s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings at 6 months showed no abnormality
OCTA findings at 12 months showed hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels
OCTA findings at 15 months showed increased hyperreflective tissues with angiogenic sprouts
OCTA findings at 18 months showed development in area of preexisting proliferation
OCTA findings at 21 months showed enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Fluorescein Angiography at 21 months showed dendritic vascular-like structures

shortlist.label: retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: OCTA findings show hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts, consistent with retinal vasculitis

shortlist.label: uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Macular edema and retinal vascular changes are consistent with uveitis

shortlist.label: vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic vasculitis can cause retinal vascular changes and macular edema

shortlist.label: sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sarcoidosis can cause uveitis, macular edema, and retinal vascular changes

shortlist.label: harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Harada disease can cause panuveitis, macular edema, and retinal vascular changes

raw.rationale: The sequential development of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA, along with the presence of dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography, suggests a chronic inflammatory condition. Sarcoidosis is known to cause granulomatous inflammation that can lead to neovascularization and is consistent with the patient's age and the gradual progression of findings.

rejected.label: retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: While retinal vasculitis could explain some findings, it typically presents with more acute inflammation and does not fully account for the gradual development of neovascularization seen in this case.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: Uveitis is a broader term that encompasses inflammation of the uveal tract, but it does not specifically explain the neovascularization and the pattern of progression observed in this patient.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: Vasculitis is a systemic condition that can affect various parts of the body, including the eyes. However, the specific pattern of neovascularization and the lack of systemic symptoms make it less likely than sarcoidosis.

rejected.label: harada disease
rejected.why: Harada disease (Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease) is a form of panuveitis that can cause granulomatous inflammation, but it typically presents with more severe and widespread ocular and systemic symptoms than described in this case.
